dept.tagline: Both 136-credit degrees - BSEEE and BSECE - on one map with every printed prerequisite, the three-part Final Year Design Project counted down, and a tracker that does the CGPA math on BRACU's own scale.

skills: Year 1
Circuit analysis by hand until nodal and mesh are automatic (EEE 101 / ECE 101, then EEE 203 / ECE 203).
A circuit simulator: build every EEE 101L experiment in it before you touch the bench.
Programming from EEE 103 / ECE 103 used on a real problem - plot a result, solve an equation, automate a calculation.
Bench basics: multimeter, oscilloscope, function generator, breadboard - the 1-credit lab courses mark you on them.
Year 2
Electronics you can debug: diodes, transistors, op-amps (EEE 205 / ECE 205 with its lab).
Numerical work in code for EEE 282 / ECE 282 Numerical Techniques - a root-finder and an integrator you wrote yourself.
Digital logic from truth table to working hardware (EEE 283 / ECE 283 and its lab).
Signals and transforms in software before the exam (EEE 243 / ECE 243, built on MAT 216).
Year 3
One microcontroller platform taken to a finished device (EEE 373 / ECE 373 Embedded Systems Design).
Control and electronic design in a simulator: EEE 305, EEE 308 and the 1-credit EEE 382 Modelling and Simulation (ECE: the same numbers).
EEE: machines and power-system calculations with per-unit values (EEE 221, EEE 321). ECE: a VLSI design flow and a communication link you measured (ECE 411, ECE 341).
A project plan with a budget and a schedule - EEE 359 / ECE 359 Engineering Project Management is the course for it.
Year 4
A Final Year Design Project (EEE 499P / D / C or ECE 499P / D / C) with requirements, alternatives, a budget, test results and a defence.
The toolchain of your specialisation area: power-system study tools, device and IC design tools, a communications toolbox or an embedded stack.
Technical writing: a report someone else could rebuild your project from; EEE 369 / ECE 369 Professional Practice covers the ethics around it.
One outside proof: an internship, a paper or poster, a competition placing, or EEE 498 / ECE 498 Directed Research.
dept.career_intro: Two degrees share this department. The BSEEE keeps Energy Conversion, Power Systems, Electrical Service Design and Machine Learning in its core; the BSECE replaces them with VLSI Design, Wireless and Mobile Communications and Digital Communications. Your specialisation area and your Final Year Design Project are the two loudest signals on your CV, so point them the same way. These are common directions, not BRACU rules.
careers: Power generation, transmission and distribution
Operating, planning and protecting the grid in public utilities and private power producers.
EEE's Power area (EEE 425 Switchgear and Protection, EEE 433 Power Systems II, EEE 429 Power System Operation and Control), EEE 221 and EEE 321 solid, recruitment-exam practice for utility jobs.
Electronics, VLSI and semiconductors
Device, circuit and chip design or testing; electronics manufacturing.
EEE 308 / ECE 308 and EEE 309 / ECE 309 strong; ECE 411 VLSI Design (ECE core), ECE 413 Digital System Design, ECE 415 Analog Integrated Circuit Design; the Electronics area in either degree.
Telecommunications, networks and RF
Network planning, optimisation and RF engineering with operators and vendors.
ECE 341, ECE 441 and ECE 445 (ECE core); ECE 349 Microwave Engineering, ECE 465 Computer Networks, ECE 487 Antennas and Propagation; EEE's Communication and Network area.
Embedded systems, robotics and IoT
Firmware, control and instrumentation for products and factories.
EEE 283 / ECE 283, EEE 373 / ECE 373 and a working device; EEE's Robotics and Intelligent System area; the Robotics Club (ROBU).
Renewable energy
Designing and commissioning solar and storage systems.
EEE 435 Renewable Energy Systems and EEE 421 Power Electronics (EEE); ECE 409 Solar Cell and Systems and ECE 421 (ECE); a sizing study for a real site.
Building services and consultancy
Electrical design for buildings: loads, wiring, protection, lighting.
EEE 384 Electrical Service Design (1 credit, EEE core) taken seriously, EEE 321, drafting skills and a complete design set.
Software, data and machine learning
Many EEE and ECE graduates move into software, data or machine learning.
EEE 103 / ECE 103 plus a second language on your own, EEE 282, EEE 385 Machine Learning (EEE core), one deployed project.
Research and higher study
A master's or PhD, then research, teaching or advanced industry roles.
CGPA, EEE 498 / ECE 498 Directed Research (the FAQ's research route, since the design project has no thesis option), a paper or poster, two recommenders who supervised your work.
career_notes: Both degrees are 136 credits: GED 39, School Core 18, Program Core 63, Final Year Design Project 4 and Program Electives 12. The cores differ in six rows each - EEE 221/221L Energy Conversion I, EEE 321/321L Power Systems I, EEE 384 Electrical Service Design and EEE 385 Machine Learning in the BSEEE; ECE 411/411L VLSI Design, ECE 441/441L Wireless and Mobile Communications and ECE 445/445L Digital Communications in the BSECE. The codes are not interchangeable: the FAQ's answer is 'No, ECE students have to take courses with the ECE codes.'
Double major, Directed Research and the minor

The FAQ allows a double major or concentration inside the degree: 'Complete a minimum of 6 non-overlapping courses (18 credits) and associated labs from two specialized areas', at least 3 courses with labs in each. Research is not a thesis - 'There is no thesis option' in the design project - but the 3-credit elective EEE 498 / ECE 498 Directed Research. For students of other departments the department prints a 28-credit Minor in EEE (tool 7 has the list).

facts: 136 credits = University Core (GED) 39 + School Core 18 + Program Core 63 + Final Year Design Project 4 + Program Electives 12; MAT 110, PHY 111, CHE 110 and STA 201 are printed in both the GED and School Core tables but count once ("* Credits counted toward University Core (GED)"), and EEE 359 and EEE 369 are printed in both School Core and Program Core but count toward School Core.

Curriculum versions by intake (department FAQ): "Version V1: For Students intake up to Spring 2018", "Version V2: For Students intake from Summer 2018 to Fall 2019", "Version V3: For Students intake from Spring 2020 and onwards" - follow the course codes of your own version.

Final Year Design Project EEE 499 runs over three consecutive semesters as EEE 499P (1 credit, 10th semester), EEE 499D (1.5, 11th) and EEE 499C (1.5, 12th); EEE 499P needs "Minimum 100 credit hours completed" plus EEE 305/305L, EEE 341/341L, EEE 343/343L, EEE 359, EEE 369, EEE 373/373L, EEE 382, EEE 383 and EEE 384, and you may start earlier if you meet these.
"There is no thesis option" in the design project; students who want research take the 3-credit elective EEE 498 Directed Research.

Program electives: "Minimum 9 credits (3 theory courses) must be from one of the following areas" - Power, Electronics, Communication and Network or Robotics and Intelligent System - chosen as your specialization (Interdisciplinary/Emerging Topics cannot be the specialization); "The remaining credits may be taken from any of the following areas".
"Students must take relevant laboratory course, if any, associated with any theory courses" - a theory elective completed without its lab does not count toward the 136 credits.
Double major/concentration: "Complete a minimum of 6 non-overlapping courses (18 credits) and associated labs from two specialized areas", at least 3 courses (9 credits) with labs in each.
Since Fall 2020 the term "Course Outside Major Area (COMA)" is discontinued; a course outside the listed areas must be programme-related and approved by your advisor beforehand.

GED Open Elective (COD): "Any one (1) non-overlapping 3-credit course from the above listed Art, Humanities, Social Science, Business, and ECST group of GED"; the FAQ allows "any non-overlapping course (minimum 3 credit hours) from other departments".

Credit load (department FAQ): "Regular students should take Maximum 15 credits and Minimum 9 credits of course per semester"; fewer than 9 only in an exceptional situation with advisor approval, more than 15 only on the advisor's strong recommendation.

Every EEE undergraduate has a fixed faculty advisor (since January 2021); advisor approval is needed to complete registration each semester; the Degree Progression Checklist (DPC) is mandatory and the Degree Completion Form replaces it in the final semester.
ECE and EEE codes are not interchangeable: "No, ECE students have to take courses with the ECE codes."

The school's Recommended Course Sequence places the four GED courses ENG 102, BNG 103, HUM 103 and EMB 101 in "Semester 03 (RS)", the residential semester; "Attending Residential semester is compulsory for all BRAC University students."

Minor in EEE (for students of other departments): 28 credits = EEE 101/101L, EEE 203/203L, EEE 205/205L and EEE 308/308L (16 credits) plus 12 credits of non-overlapping 300- or 400-level EEE electives with their labs; minimum CGPA 2.00 in minor courses; up to 12 credits (3 courses) may be exempted if they already count toward the major.

University rules (Policies and Procedures page): graduation needs a minimum CGPA of 2.00 and at least 70 credits earned at BRAC University; a CGPA below 2.0 means probation with up to three consecutive semesters to recover; the degree must be finished within 8 years of first admission (minimum 3 years).

Admission (Undergraduate Admission page): SSC and HSC minimum GPA 3.5 with an HSC "B" grade in Physics & Mathematics (A-level "C"), or IB-DP score 24 with MAT and PHY at HL/SL 4; the admission test has "English (Composition and MCQ), Mathematics MCQ, Higher Mathematics MCQ and Physics MCQ" and each sub-section must be passed separately; applicants without HSC/A-level Chemistry "will have to take a remedial course on Chemistry".
Placement (Freshman Enrollment page): the admission test may prescribe ENG 091, MAT 091 and MAT 092 (non-credit) before ENG 101/ENG 102 (3 credits each); a freshman takes up to four courses in total.

Fees (Tuition and Fees page, new students from Spring 2027): tuition Tk. 8,250 per credit, admission fee Tk. 33,900 (one time), semester fee Tk. 10,520 ("All other Program" row - EEE and ECE are not named), library membership Tk. 2,500 (one time); "Fees can be changed as per the decision of the university."
Three semesters a year - Spring, Summer and Fall (Academic Dates page).

book.text: Read this first

This planner puts your whole EEE degree in one place: every published course, the rules that move your CGPA, the dates that cost money, and a working page for every week of the semester - on your phone, offline, with the arithmetic done for you.
What you are holding

items: **Degree** - the Bachelor of Science in Electrical and Electronic Engineering and Bachelor of Science in Electronic and Communication Engineering as BRACU prints it: every course, its credits and its prerequisite. Pick a semester and a grade per course and the CGPA, the credit map, the Ready / Locked checks and your semester-by-semester plan follow.
**CGPA** - the grading scale, a quick semester GPA, what it takes to reach a target, a retake what-if on BRACU's own rule, and the CGPA lines that decide waivers and standing.
**Money** - this semester's bill at the published rates, the whole degree roughly, and the dates that cost money with a countdown you can send to your calendar.
**Semester** - deadlines and tasks, your routine with a clash check, and the working pages of a semester (set-up, course pages, check-ins, finals plan), one set per semester.
**Toolkit** - the tools this department's work actually needs, with logs and calculators that count and flag as you type.
**Rules** - BRACU's own grading, retake, probation, load, scholarship and fee rules, with the source named under each.
**More** - clubs and careers, the printable pages, an assignment cover page, the Excel version of the tracker, and your backup.

book.text: What it is not

items: It is **not an official BRACU document**. Nobody at the university wrote, checked or approved it.
It does **not replace your advisor**, your advising sheet or the student portal. Those decide what counts toward your degree.

It is **a snapshot**. Course lists, fees, CGPA lines and dates were read from BRACU's own web pages on 20 October 2026. Universities change these. When a notice and this planner disagree - cross the old line out here, and the notice wins.

book.text: Start in 15 minutes

items: On **Home**, type your name, the semester you were admitted in and the semester you are in now.
On **Degree**, pick the semester and the grade of every course you have passed. Your CGPA appears at once, and every course shows Ready, Locked or Open.
On **Money**, type this semester's fee and drop dates from the Registrar's calendar; they count down on Home.
On **Semester**, put your sections into the routine and your deadlines into the task list.
Open the **Toolkit** when the work starts: labs, projects, cases, the final-year runway.

book.text: Your data

Everything you type stays in this browser on this device - nothing is sent anywhere, there is no account and no internet is needed. That also means a cleared browser or a new phone starts empty. So, now and then, open **More** and tap **Save this planner with my data inside**: you get this same file back with everything you have typed written into it. Keep that copy - open it on a laptop, send it to a new phone, or hand it to next semester's you.

If a browser refuses to keep your data between visits (some phones open files in a way that forgets), Home tells you so and offers the same button. Your planner is then simply the latest copy you saved.

the Rules tab - Rules that move your CGPA and your money

Most students learn these rules by breaking one. Read them once now. Everything here is taken from BRAC University's published pages as they stood in October 2026; the source is named under each section.
The grading scale
BRAC University's undergraduate scale, in force since Fall 2020. Both A+ and A carry the full 4.0.
A+ to D- are passing grades. F is failing: it earns no credit and counts as zero in your GPA.
How your GPA and CGPA are worked out

Every course gives you **quality points = credits x grade point**. Add the quality points for a semester and divide by the credits you attempted for a letter grade: that is your semester GPA. Do the same across all semesters and you have your CGPA. The policy page prints the same formula: the sum of (grade points x credits) over the credits attempted.
Three things students get wrong

items: **An F stays in the sum until it is retaken.** It adds credits to the bottom of the fraction and nothing to the top.
**A D- passes, but it costs you.** A 3-credit D- is 2.1 quality points against 12.0 for an A - and a grade of B- or below is what the repeat rule exists for.
**W, I, P and AU never enter the GPA.** A W costs you the fee and the semester's work, not grade points.

book.text: 5. Circuits on paper: the method and the error log

Most marks lost in EEE 101, 203, 205 and 308 - and in the ECE courses with the same numbers - are not lost to theory. They go to signs, units and unlabelled diagrams. Use the same six steps on every problem, from Electrical Circuits I to Signals and Systems and Electromagnetic Waves and Fields.

items: **Redraw** the circuit cleanly. Label every node, every current with a direction, every voltage with a polarity.
**Choose the method** before you write an equation: nodal, mesh, superposition, Thevenin/Norton, phasors, small-signal model, Laplace.
**Write the equations** in symbols first. Substitute numbers only at the end.
**Carry units** through every line. Convert kilo, milli and micro once, at the start.
**Sanity-check**: power supplied equals power absorbed; a voltage across a short is zero; the answer has a believable size.
**Box the answer** with its unit and, for AC, its form (rms or peak, polar or rectangular).
